title: Recommendations
brief: Every page shows a row of things the visitor might like. A ranking model builds each row, but the model is slow and costly. The row must appear instantly, even when the model is having a bad day.

clarify.q: Does the row need to be exactly right for this second?
clarify.a: No. A list computed a few hours ago is fine for most people.

clarify.q: What if the model is slow or down?
clarify.a: Show a simple popular-items row. A generic row is far better than a blank space.

clarify.q: Is it a problem if two people see the same row?
clarify.a: No. Many people share a similar taste group, so shared answers are fine.

notes: A ranking call takes about 50 ms of model time (approx.).
Click events help tomorrow's lists but need not be real-time.

hints: Ranking is expensive. Which rows can be reused between visits?
Cache rows for a long time and put a circuit breaker before the model so a slow model does not drag every page.
Servers, distributed cache with collapse-misses, circuit breaker, recommender with a feature store, key-value store. Keep a popular-items path that skips the model.

editorial.summary: Rank once, reuse many times. Rows are cached for hours. If the model slows down, a circuit breaker stops waiting and the page falls back to a popular row stored beside it.

designs.name: Cache, breaker, fallback
designs.why: The cache absorbs nearly all reads. Misses go through a circuit breaker to the recommender. If the breaker opens, misses fall back to precomputed popular lists, so pages stay fast.

tradeoffs: A longer cache time cuts model cost but shows older tastes. A new item takes a while to appear.
The breaker trades quality for speed: a generic row is shown when the model is slow.
Collapsing misses protects the model when the cache is emptied.
Click events feed tomorrow's model off the fast path, so a logging issue cannot slow a page.
editorial.realWorld: Large shops and video services precompute most recommendations offline and serve them from memory. Live ranking is limited to a few hundred candidates (approx.).
